confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'it is likely that moisture has tracked underneath the ceramic glass and caused a short circuit in the control electronics'

rationale: The assistant misread Er03 as a control-system short-circuit from moisture under the glass, when on this AEG hob it is the touch-control safety cut-off triggered by liquid on the panel; it never asked whether the controls were wet or covered. The practical advice (isolate, wipe, dry, retry) is safe and would eventually work, but the 24-48 hour wait is grossly excessive versus a wipe and a few minutes off at the wall, and the talk of 'permanent damage to the control PCB' is unsupported and alarming. No part was pushed and nothing unsafe was advised, but the customer leaves without the correct explanation or confirmation that the hob is fine once dry.
